How It Works

How Shortcodes works in Kenya

From registration to live delivery, here is what working with MobiWave looks like.

  1. 1

    Choose shared or dedicated

    Shared shortcodes are live fast on a sub-keyword of MobiWave’s allocated code. Dedicated codes are yours alone for full branding and unrestricted keyword control.

  2. 2

    Register your sender ID (CAK)

    We handle alphanumeric sender ID registration with Safaricom, Airtel and Telkom under the CAK-aligned framework during onboarding — at no extra admin fee. Most are approved in 1–3 business days.

  3. 3

    Configure keywords & auto-replies

    Set up keyword routing, auto-responders and subscription logic in the dashboard or via API. Inbound messages post to your webhook in real time.

  4. 4

    Launch your campaign

    Publish the shortcode and sender ID across your marketing. Track inbound volume, opt-ins and replies from one console.

  5. 5

    Stay compliant

    We maintain the opt-in / opt-out ledger and enforce STOP-to-unsubscribe so every two-way flow stays within ODPC and CAK rules.

  6. 6

    Bundle with SMS, USSD & WhatsApp

    Add bulk SMS, USSD menus and WhatsApp to the same MobiWave account — one billing line, one support contact.

Frequently Asked Questions

Shortcodes questions, answered.

The practical questions Kenyan organisations ask about shortcodes, with straight answers and KES pricing where it applies.

Still have a question? Talk to us →

Alphanumeric sender IDs in Kenya are registered with the mobile networks under the Communications Authority of Kenya (CAK) framework. MobiWave handles registration with Safaricom, Airtel and Telkom during onboarding at no extra admin fee. You will need a signed, stamped authorisation letter on company letterhead; most sender IDs are approved within 1–3 business days.
